Section: 2. Business Background
2. Business Background
The organization currently manages employee onboarding through email, HR spreadsheets and separate IT and Facilities request queues. Hiring Managers submit new-hire information and documents, after which HR Operations, Compliance, IT Access, Facilities and Payroll perform separate checks and setup activities. Employee data is repeatedly entered into different records.
A typical employee onboarding cycle takes seven business days from request submission to readiness for the employee's first day. Delays are concentrated around incomplete identity or employment documents, background or compliance verification, access approvals and equipment provisioning. Managers have limited visibility into outstanding onboarding tasks.

Section: 3. Business Problem Statement
3. Business Problem Statement
The current process has the following limitations:
New-hire personal and employment data are re-entered between HR, IT and Facilities processes.
Identity, tax and employment documents are exchanged through email or shared folders.
HR Operations spends time chasing missing information from hiring managers.
Access approvals and provisioning dependencies are tracked separately from HR onboarding.
Equipment and workplace setup tasks are followed up manually and can delay employee readiness.
Managers cannot reliably identify new hires approaching their onboarding SLA.

Section: 4. Business Objectives
4. Business Objectives
ID | Objective | Success Measure
BO-01 | Reduce end-to-end employee onboarding cycle time. | Reduce average cycle time from 7 business days to 2 business days.
BO-02 | Reduce manual operational effort. | Achieve at least 60% reduction in manual onboarding effort.
BO-03 | Improve onboarding status visibility. | Provide role-based, near-real-time onboarding status and aging views.
BO-04 | Strengthen onboarding compliance adherence. | Prevent access provisioning when required identity, employment or compliance checks are incomplete.
BO-05 | Provide full auditability. | Capture timestamped onboarding changes, document actions, approvals and provisioning decisions.

Section: 5. Scope
5. Scope

Section: 5.1 In Scope
5.1 In Scope
New employee onboarding requests
Employee, employment and manager data capture
Identity, tax and employment document upload and validation
Compliance verification and access approval routing
IT, equipment and workplace setup task tracking
Onboarding status notifications, dashboards and standard reports
Role-based approval, rejection and return actions

Section: 5.2 Out of Scope
5.2 Out of Scope
Changes to payroll calculation logic.
Changes to enterprise identity platform configuration.
Maintenance of existing employee master data.
Migration of historical onboarding records beyond the agreed POC sample set.

Section: 7. Current Process
7. Current Process
Step | Current Activity
1 | Hiring Manager submits employee details and supporting documents to HR Operations by email or shared folder.
2 | HR Operations checks completeness and re-enters employee information into onboarding trackers.
3 | HR or Compliance performs identity, employment and required screening checks.
4 | IT determines required system access and equipment based on employee role.
5 | Approvers communicate approval, rejection or additional-information requests through email.
6 | IT and Facilities complete access, equipment and workplace setup after required approvals.
7 | HR and Hiring Manager are notified when the employee is ready for onboarding completion.

Section: 8. Future-State Business Requirements
8. Future-State Business Requirements
BR-001  Employee Onboarding Registration
The solution shall allow authorized Hiring Managers and HR Operations users to create, save and submit a new employee onboarding request through a web-based interface.
BR-002  Employee Document Upload
The solution shall support upload of identity evidence, employment contracts, tax documents, certifications and other configured onboarding documents.
BR-003  Mandatory Employee Document Validation
The solution shall verify that mandatory identity and employment documents for the selected employee type and jurisdiction are available before verification can be completed.
BR-004  Onboarding Workflow Management
The solution shall route onboarding tasks to HR Operations, Compliance, IT Access and Facilities according to configured role, location and employment rules.
BR-005  Onboarding Approval Actions
Authorized approvers shall be able to approve, reject or return an onboarding request for additional information, with mandatory comments where configured.
BR-006  Onboarding Notifications

Section: 8. Future-State Business Requirements
BR-006  Onboarding Notifications
The solution shall notify relevant users when a task is assigned, returned, approved, rejected, overdue or completed.
BR-007  Onboarding Status Visibility
Authorized users shall be able to view onboarding stage, responsible owner, outstanding tasks, aging and next action.
BR-008  Onboarding Audit Trail
The solution shall maintain an immutable history of submissions, employee-data changes, document actions, approvals, provisioning decisions and status transitions.
BR-009  Onboarding Search and Reporting
Users shall be able to search onboarding requests and generate standard reports by status, age, employee type, location and owning team.
BR-010  Onboarding Exception Handling
The solution shall place an onboarding request on hold when mandatory information is missing or a verification fails, and shall record the reason.

Section: 9. Functional Requirements
9. Functional Requirements
ID | Functional Requirement | Priority
FR-001 | Create, save as draft, edit and submit an employee onboarding request. | Must
FR-002 | Capture employee, employment, manager, location, start date, role and department information. | Must
FR-003 | Upload, classify, preview, replace and download onboarding supporting documents. | Must
FR-004 | Validate mandatory employee fields and required identity or employment documents before submission. | Must
FR-005 | Assign and reassign onboarding tasks to authorized users or groups. | Must
FR-006 | Record approve, reject, return and request-information decisions. | Must
FR-007 | Display onboarding stage, pending tasks, owner and aging. | Must
FR-008 | Send email notifications based on configurable onboarding events. | Should
FR-009 | Search onboarding requests using request ID, employee name, department, status and date range. | Must
FR-010 | Generate onboarding volume, status, aging and SLA reports. | Should
FR-011 | Export authorized onboarding report results to a standard downloadable format. | Could
FR-012 | Capture a complete audit history for each onboarding request. | Must

Section: 10. Non-Functional Requirements
10. Non-Functional Requirements
ID | Category | Requirement
NFR-001 | Availability | The production solution shall target 99.9% monthly service availability, excluding agreed maintenance windows.
NFR-002 | Performance | For normal operating load, standard application pages shall respond within 3 seconds for 95% of requests.
NFR-003 | Capacity | The solution shall support up to 500 concurrent users and allow future scaling.
NFR-004 | Security | Access shall use corporate authentication and role-based authorization with least-privilege principles.
NFR-005 | Privacy | Borrower, financial and collateral information shall be handled in accordance with applicable data protection and organizational privacy requirements.
NFR-006 | Auditability | Credit and workflow events shall be logged with user, timestamp, action, decision and outcome.
NFR-007 | Retention | Loan processing records shall be retained for seven years unless a different approved schedule applies.
NFR-008 | Accessibility | Core user journeys shall support accessible keyboard navigation and readable screen content.

Section: 11. Business Rules
11. Business Rules
Rule ID | Business Rule
RULE-001 | All mandatory identity and employment documents must be present before verification can be completed.
RULE-002 | An employee requiring privileged system access requires designated IT access approval in addition to HR approval.
RULE-003 | A request with missing mandatory information shall be placed on hold and returned to the requestor.
RULE-004 | Every approval, rejection and return decision shall include a timestamp and decision-maker identity.
RULE-005 | Access provisioning shall not begin until required HR and Compliance approvals are recorded.
RULE-006 | A rejection shall require a reason and shall close the active workflow unless reopened by an authorized role.
RULE-007 | Only authorized users may view or download documents containing personal employee information.
RULE-008 | Overdue onboarding tasks shall trigger reminders according to the configured SLA schedule.

Section: 12. Assumptions
12. Assumptions
All POC users have valid corporate identities.
Credit scoring, KYC and risk services can be represented by mock services if live APIs are unavailable.
Email notification infrastructure is available for integration or simulation.
POC loan documents use synthetic or anonymized data only.
Business users will provide feedback and acceptance decisions for the POC scenarios.

Section: 13. Constraints
13. Constraints
The target solution shall use approved Azure services and organizational development standards.
Borrower and financial data shall remain within approved data regions and repositories.
The POC shall not use production lending credentials or confidential customer data.
Access to SharePoint, Teams, Jira or Azure DevOps is subject to approved permissions and DLP controls.
Human review is required before generated DRS and backlog items are treated as approved artefacts.

Section: 14. Acceptance Criteria
14. Acceptance Criteria
ID | Acceptance Criterion | Mapped Requirement
AC-001 | Given an authorized Hiring Manager, when mandatory employee and employment information is entered, then the user can save and submit an onboarding request. | BR-001 / FR-001
AC-002 | Given a selected employee type, when the user uploads required identity and employment documents, then each document is recorded against the request. | BR-002 / FR-003
AC-003 | Given a missing mandatory identity document, when the user attempts to progress the request, then progression is blocked and the missing document is identified. | BR-003 / FR-004
AC-004 | Given a submitted onboarding request, when role and location workflow rules are evaluated, then the appropriate HR or Compliance task is assigned. | BR-004 / FR-005
AC-005 | Given an assigned approver, when the approver selects approve, reject or return, then the decision and comments are recorded and the workflow transitions. | BR-005 / FR-006

Section: 14. Acceptance Criteria
AC-006 | Given a configured approval event, when the event occurs, then the intended recipient receives a notification containing the loan application identifier and required action. | BR-006 / FR-008
AC-007 | Given an authorized user, when the loan application is opened, then stage, owner, aging and outstanding conditions are visible. | BR-007 / FR-007
AC-008 | Given a saved credit decision, when the audit history is opened, then the user, timestamp, decision and outcome are displayed. | BR-008 / FR-012
AC-009 | Given search criteria, when the user searches loans, then matching authorized applications are returned and can be filtered. | BR-009 / FR-009
AC-010 | Given a failed verification, when the request is placed on hold, then the hold reason and responsible owner are recorded. | BR-010 / FR-004
